column7: SHARE-CAS-1 (REVIEW-2 residual on #3367): on PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED UpdateSharePermission classified its change (widens or not) from an unlocked in-transaction read and then wrote the share, so a narrowing on another replica committing in between turned an update classified neutral (write to write) into write over read with only a best-effort audit row (none during an audit outage). The read is now LockShareRecordForUpdate (FOR UPDATE), so the concurrent update waits and applies after the commit; a preserved expiry and the expired-share check use the same locked row. Red without the fix: the narrowing is undone and the rows [write->read, write->write] cannot explain the final write; the preserved-expiry sibling (TestCTAReview_UpdateSharePermission_PreservedExpiryVsConcurrentShortening_CrossReplicaPostgres) writes the 48h expiry back over the 1h one. Default-CI guards: TestUpdateSharePermission_ClassifiesFromALockedRead, TestLockShareRecordForUpdate_DialectMatchedLocking. SQLite has no window (BEGIN IMMEDIATE).
